assumptions: The founder keeps the corporate job and limits business work to five hours per day until objective traction and runway conditions are met.

Qualified customs specialists, rather than the founder or software alone, own professional judgments, representation, and escalations; the service does not assume unverified authority to act as a customs representative.
The inherited 75000 PLN capital estimate is staged behind paid demand evidence, and no parental capital is assumed.
No particular importer vertical, price, margin, renewal rate, acquisition cost, case frequency, or valuation is assumed to be attractive without evidence.
Private product facts and case outcomes can be reused only when the customer grants explicit contractual permission; no proprietary dataset is assumed at launch.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The concept correctly moves the paid value away from free filing and increasingly commoditized code lookup toward complete product-fact development, defensible reasoning, monitoring, and exception handling. A direct relationship in one vertical could make recurring fact templates and case history useful, but the research does not yet establish that this is an overlooked control point rather than a narrower packaging of services incumbents already provide.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Classification can affect duties, licences, restrictions, and origin requirements, and incomplete facts can invalidate a binding decision, so difficult new-SKU and dispute cases can carry meaningful stakes. However, the frequency and financial severity of those cases within any proposed vertical, budget ownership, willingness to buy an annual contract, and renewal behavior are unknown; the official Polish filing itself is free.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: An annual monitoring contract plus separately priced expert escalations can combine recurring revenue with high-value case work, and reusable vertical templates could spread acquisition and specialist cost. No evidence yet supports price, gross margin, expert hours, insurance and liability cost, CAC, payback, retention, case density, or operating leverage. Expert review and support may keep the model service-heavy, and there is not yet a credible quantified path or timing to the founder's net-worth target.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A single repeat-SKU importer vertical is appropriately narrow in principle and the EU customs context provides a broad eventual market. The beachhead is not actually selected, and no evidence establishes reachable account density, recurring difficult-classification volume, insufficient internal capability, or an economically meaningful serviceable segment in any one vertical.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Avalara, eClear, TariffPilot, and logistics providers already cover substantial portions of automated research, bulk processing, APIs, reasoning, expert review, and customs support. Vertical focus and direct importer ownership may improve relevance, but there is no demonstrated exclusive access, superior performance, embedded workflow position, or partner right that would support a dominant segment position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven vertical workflow could extend into adjacent product categories, rule-change monitoring, audit support, disputes, landed-cost decisions, and additional EU geographies. Transfer is only moderate because product facts, classification expertise, liability, and acquisition relationships can be vertical-specific, while contractual limits may prevent data reuse across customers or segments.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned product-fact templates, accumulated review questions, case history, and integration into a recurring importer workflow could create learning effects and switching cost. Those advantages are conditional on explicit reuse rights, sufficient case volume, and renewals; verified outcomes arrive slowly, public rulings and official research remain accessible, and established providers can copy a vertical workflow.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The proposed combination of structured intake, qualified expert review, evidence packs, monitoring, and exception support could be safer and more convenient than a generic code recommender. The research contains no accuracy, turnaround, cost, risk-reduction, or user-experience benchmark showing a material advantage over incumbent managed services or an importer's existing customs advisers.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Frequently updated tariff information, persistent classification complexity, and capable AI tooling make structured monitoring and evidence assembly feasible now. The same evidence shows that several vendors already exploit these enablers, and no new regulatory deadline, cost discontinuity, or channel opening uniquely favors this entrant.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Direct account-based outreach in one vertical is coherent and removes dependence on a forwarder that may substitute its own consulting; optional referrals preserve flexibility. Conversion, sales cycle, acquisition cost, reachable account density, and a scalable lead source are all unknown, while enterprise compliance sales may be slow and socially demanding for a part-time founder.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data, AI, and automation skills fit the workflow product, the stated initial capital is within available funds, and qualified expertise can in principle be contracted. Execution still depends on specialist availability and cost, insurance and liability allocation, accurate customer facts, representation rules, direct sales, customer data permissions, and keeping expert delivery compatible with part-time operation. These are material but not evidenced as impossible.

main_structural_strength: The model owns the importer renewal relationship and focuses qualified experts and software on difficult evidence, monitoring, and exception workflows rather than trying to monetize free filing or generic code prediction. If one vertical supplies repeat cases, this structure can reuse product-fact work and make the service progressively more useful.
primary_score_limiter: The business has no evidence-selected beachhead or demonstrated control point beyond a direct contract: the same unknown vertical must supply sufficient complex-case density, paid annual demand, affordable acquisition, data-use rights, and repeatable expert margins despite mature overlapping incumbents.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Avalara already combines automated and managed classification, APIs, post-audit support, human experts, and large-catalogue scale, while eClear and TariffPilot provide further overlapping AI and reasoning workflows; this directly challenges the proposed offer's differentiation and domination potential.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: For one named vertical: importer records showing recurring difficult-case frequency and avoidable loss; multiple paid annual pilots with observed conversion and sales cycle; repeat use or renewal; measured expert hours, contribution margin, liability and support cost, CAC and payback; signed permission for the intended de-identified reuse; and benchmarked accuracy, turnaround, or risk reduction versus incumbent tools and current advisers.
highest_value_structural_change: Turn the stand-alone assurance contract into an embedded SKU-governance layer for one named vertical's PIM or ERP onboarding workflow, with portfolio-based recurring pricing, continuous rule-change monitoring, explicit de-identified outcome rights, and qualified-expert escalation. That would make the control point a recurring operational workflow and proprietary feedback loop rather than sporadic case delivery.
